a-skill-teaches-the-class-of-problem.header: A skill teaches the class of problem and reads the instance
a-skill-teaches-the-class-of-problem.description: a skill "should teach the agent how to approach a class of problems, not what to produce for a specific instance"; the example reads the schema from references/schema.yaml instead of writing joins into the skill [1]. Claude Code offers $'{'CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR'}' so a skill can reference project files independent of where it is installed [2].

the-card-points.title: The card points
the-card-points.script: Here is the mistake from before, fixed. The skill no longer says 40 metres. Its step says "descend to the depth in today's dive plan", and that dive plan is a project file the skill reads when the step runs: site 4, 40 metres, site 7, 120 metres.

same-card-any-site.title: Same card, any site
same-card-any-site.script: Replay site 7. It is the same skill with no edit, and this time the robot reaches the seabed at 120 metres. The procedure stayed put and the site details lived in the project file, which is your third step in miniature: decide where the project details live.

for-developers.title: For developers
for-developers.script: In the coding-agent view the step names a project file, say CONTEXT.md, and the agent reads it when that step runs. For everyone else, it is any document in your project that the skill tells the model to read.
